$doc: The definition row's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component definition-row` block in css/components.css and of dist/react/definition-row.tsx. THIS BLOCK USED TO BE HALF OF `row`, and the split is why it can be a definition at all. One component owned two banners: a clickable index entry (`.idx__row`) and a term-and-definition pair (`.tools__row`), and they shared a name because both are full-width list rows and nothing else. The project half needs `.idx li:last-child .idx__row` — a positional in the MIDDLE of a descendant path, which no closure in this format reaches — so it stays authored under its own marker. This half needs a part, a position, two scoped parts and one named condition, all of which are vocabulary that already exists. Splitting a component is a MAJOR change and the contract said so; what it bought is that the half that can be data is data, instead of both halves waiting on the half that cannot.

note: The block root. A `<dl>` stacks its rows in normal flow anyway, so the
visual result is identical — but grid makes the wrapper the thing that
owns the stack, which is what `.tools__row` is a row OF. Without a rule
here the class shipped on four pages meant nothing at all.
rules.$doc: One declaration, and the note above it is the whole argument for having it: the wrapper is what the rows are rows of. The note is a RULE note because it explains why the rule exists rather than what the declaration does.

rules.name: row
rules.$doc: One term-and-definition pair, laid out as a two-track grid: a term track that may shrink to 9rem and grow to 14rem, and the definition taking the rest. The `<div>` wrapping each dt/dd pair is the markup's, so that the outer `<dl>` has one box per row to stack — the same shape `profile` uses, and for the same reason.

rules.name: closing
rules.$doc: The last row drops its rule, so the list ends on the section's own edge rather than on a line inside it. The same `last` the fact row and the entry use, and the same reason: no row knows how many siblings it has, and the markup should not have to say.

rules.name: term
rules.$doc: The skill group's name, in the display family at body size and uppercase — a heading for the line beside it rather than a label above it, which is what `align-self: center` records: the term sits on the optical middle of a definition that may run to three lines.

rules.name: value
rules.$doc: The list of tools. One declaration: the `<dd>`'s own margin is already off in the foundation reset, and its colour is the page's body ink.

Stacked. A term track that has shrunk to 9rem leaves a definition column too narrow to read, so below 620px the pair becomes two lines — and the gap goes with it: `space-7` is the air between two things side by side, and stacked it would put a paragraph's worth of it between a heading and the line it heads.
